summary: Global trade compliance domain foundation adds trade-party screening metadata, trade-item classification metadata, export-control assessment metadata, customs-declaration preparation metadata, landed-cost simulation metadata, and SAP GTS parity-map linkage while explicitly refusing live denied-party screening, government list downloads, regulatory content subscriptions, legal rulings, customs/export filing, broker submission, shipment/order/inventory/accounting mutation, Workflow execution, cloud deployment, and runtime audit-chain claims.
non_claims: no live denied-party or sanctions-provider network call
no production SAP GTS parity claim

findings: The slice is additive and isolates global-trade compliance invariants in a flat microservice crate rather than widening Enterprise Suite into a GTS/ERP monolith.
The API remains pure data-in/data-out with no I/O, durable state, denied-party provider, government filing, broker network, document archive, Workflow execution, or mutation-side runtime.

claims_allowed: ERP parity-map linkage for SAP GTS
findings: Independent scaling and deployment remain future adapter/runtime work; this slice only creates the pure domain foundation.

F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Tests fail if missing party screening, missing item classification, missing export-control assessment, missing customs declaration, compliance holds, invalid country/HS/ECCN/incoterm/procedure values, unsafe refs, credential-shaped refs, invalid amounts, invalid duty rates, or zero quantities are accepted.
findings: Positive party-to-item-to-export-control-to-customs-to-landed-cost flow and negative guard rails are covered.
Types map directly to party screening, product classification, export control, customs declarations, and landed-cost concepts common to global-trade systems.

alternatives_named: leave GTS as a parity gap
build live GTS/customs filing runtime now
add global-trade compliance domain foundation first
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: A flat domain foundation gives SAP GTS parity a service-owned first write path while keeping live sanctions providers, regulatory content, legal rulings, customs/export filings, broker networks, Workflow, document archive runtimes, mutation-side integrations, and cloud adapters out of scope.
rejected_reasons: Leaving GTS as a gap weakens ERP parity after CRM, SCM/APO, PM, QM, PP, warehouse, procurement, and treasury foundations landed.

Live global-trade runtime requires denied-party providers, regulatory-content subscriptions, government/broker integrations, durable document storage, operational SLOs, and cloud evidence beyond this slice.

findings: No credentials, external network calls, denied-party provider calls, customs filings, broker submissions, shipment/order/inventory/accounting mutations, or Workflow dispatches are introduced.
List, source, and audit refs reject traversal, whitespace/control, and credential-shaped strings.
